newsitem.title: UK: Stg climbs against mark, dollar in quiet Europe.
newsitem.headline: Stg climbs against mark, dollar in quiet Europe.

text.p: Sterling advanced steadily to session highs against the German mark, dollar and yen on Friday in cautious trade ahead of interest rate decisions in Germany and the United States next week.
"Interest rate concerns are guiding the market," David Bloom, currency strategist at HSBC James Capel said. "People are just trading around for now, getting in position."
Dealers said sterling activity was very light with much of Europe on holiday today.

Market focus remained on next Tuesday's German repo tender amid heightened speculation the Bundesbank could engineer a German rate rise. Also on Tuesday, the policy-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting deliberates interest rates but a rate hike here is seen more remote, said analysts.
The pound stood at 2.9441/51 marks after touching an earlier peak of 2.9494, just shy of key chart resistance at 2.95 marks. It stood at 2.9295/9305 late Thursday in Europe.

Cable was also firmer at $1.5997/08 after triggering stops on its break of week-old resistance around $1.5940 but was held at another chart level just above $1.60. It traded at $1.5869/74 late Thursday.
"The market is very thin today, and with with no fresh news it's only technical factors that have been steering the pound," said a UK bank dealer.
Bundesbank officials have expressed concern over the last week at inflationary pressures in the German economy, prompting renewed speculation of a Buba rate rise as soon as next week.
James Barty, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, said he felt the German central bank would not push up its rates soon. "Sterling is likely to get a lift from that."
Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said in a newspaper interview the Buba was concerned about inflation and keeping a close eye on any "exaggerated" market moves.
Germany, however, is reluctant to choke off nascent economic recovery by cranking up interest rates, said analysts.
One trader said that in thin trading he saw some danger of turbulence in Asian markets spilling over into Europe.

The dollar rose above 118.00 yen as money fleeing from troubled Asian currencies took sanctuary in the U.S. unit rather than the yen, already beleaguered by concerns over sluggish Japanese economic growth.

"The yen's weakness is due to more than just one factor, but it is hard to see anything positive for the yen out of the Asian currency crisis," said Kit Juckes, currency strategist at NatWest Markets in London.

Sterling also tracked higher against the yen to 189.77, its highest level in a week. By midday Europe it was still firm but more settled at 189.27/55 yen. It stood around 186.00 yen in late Thursday European trade.
